articles.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
articles.description: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
articles.summary: Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.
key_points: Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported , external .
Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training…
He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.

articles.title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years
articles.description: ﻿The UK economy grew by 0.7% in the three months to September, according to official figures.
articles.summary: ﻿The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.
key_points: Between July and September, the economy expanded by 0.7%, accelerating from the three months previously, official figures show.

Strong growth in the services sector - which includes non-physical goods such as consultancy services and hotels and restaurants - helped drive the stronger growth.

articles.description: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
articles.summary: Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal.
key_points: The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.

articles.title: From Paris to DC - why offices are being turned into apartments
articles.description: Office buildings with low occupancy rates are being transformed into flats.
articles.summary: Le Diamant office building is to close and be converted into apartments When Roland Cubin walks you round what will eventually be a new Parisian apartment you have to use your imagination.
key_points: "Here you will be in the kitchen, and here is the bathroom," says the deputy CEO of French real estate company Groupama Immobilier.
It all sounds appealing, an upmarket flat in the west of Paris, but presently the space doesn't look like one at all.
That's because it's currently a corner of one floor of a nine-storey office building called Le Diamant, where 1,800 people work.

articles.title: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
articles.description: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
articles.summary: Traditional games and stickers are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show.
key_points: The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK.
The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana.
The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between £5 and £10.
